name: Palácio Nacional de Queluz
seoTitle: Queluz Palace by Train: A Port-Day Alternative to Pena
tagline: An 18th-century royal palace near Lisbon that fits a port day far more easily than Sintra.

description.short: The 18th-century royal palace and gardens of Queluz, between Lisbon and Sintra. From the cruise terminal it is 50 to 60 minutes each way by metro, train and a short walk, or 25 to 30 minutes by taxi, with no hill or shuttle bus involved.
description.full:
Queluz is the royal palace closest to the cruise terminal and the easiest one to fit into a port day. It stands in a suburb about 15 km north-west of Jardim do Tabaco, on the railway to Sintra, and involves no shuttle bus or hill climb. If Pena is out of reach on your call, this is the realistic alternative for 18th-century royal interiors.

By public transport, walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia, take the metro Blue Line to Restauradores and walk two minutes to Rossio station. Sintra-line trains reach Queluz-Belas in about 20 minutes; from there the palace is a 10 to 15-minute walk (about 1 km) through ordinary suburban streets. Allow 50 to 60 minutes door to door each way. A taxi takes 25 to 30 minutes and makes sense on a short call or when several people share the fare.

With 1.5 to 2 hours on site, you need at least 5 hours ashore if you go by taxi, or 6 hours by train, including being back at the terminal an hour before all-aboard. On an 8-hour call there is time to add the Baixa or Belém on the way back.

Buy the Palace and Gardens ticket (13 euros); the interiors are the reason to come. The route runs through the state rooms: prioritise the Throne Room, the Music Room, the Ambassadors Room and the Don Quixote Room, where Pedro IV was born and died. Then go out to the gardens for the Tiled Canal, lined with blue-and-white azulejo panels, the Grand Cascade and the lead statues from John Cheere's London workshop.

Skip the gardens-only ticket (6 euros) unless you have no interest in interiors. Do not try to add Pena on the same day: the two together need more time than a normal port call allows. The ticket office closes from 12:00 to 13:00, but ticket machines keep working, and an online ticket for your date avoids the issue.
description.history: The estate began as a country house confiscated after 1640 and given to the Casa do Infantado, the property of the monarch's younger sons. In 1747 Prince Pedro, the future Pedro III, commissioned the architect Mateus Vicente de Oliveira to enlarge it. After his marriage to the heir to the throne, Princess Maria, was announced in 1760, the works were extended under the French architect and goldsmith Jean-Baptiste Robillion. When fire destroyed the royal complex at Ajuda in 1794, Queluz became the residence of Queen Maria I and the court until the royal family left for Brazil in 1807. Pedro IV was born and died in the Don Quixote Room. A fire in 1934 badly damaged the interior, which was later restored.
description.significance: Queluz is one of the most complete royal ensembles of 18th-century Portugal, and its rooms show the shift from Baroque to Rococo and Neoclassicism. It was the home of Maria I's court and the birthplace of Pedro IV, first emperor of Brazil. It was classified a National Monument in 1910, and since 1957 its eastern wing, the D. Maria I Pavilion, has housed foreign heads of state on official visits. Unlike the Sintra palaces, it is not part of the UNESCO-listed Cultural Landscape of Sintra.

directions.general: Located in Queluz, between Lisbon and Sintra, easily accessible by train from either city
directions.fromCruisePort: Walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia and take the metro Blue Line to Restauradores; Rossio station is a two-minute walk. Sintra-line trains from Rossio reach Queluz-Belas in about 20 minutes, then walk 10 to 15 minutes (about 1 km) to the palace. Allow 50 to 60 minutes door to door. A taxi takes about 25 to 30 minutes.
directions.publicTransport: CP Sintra line from Rossio, Entrecampos or Oriente to Queluz-Belas or Monte Abraão, each about 1 km from the palace. Carris Metropolitana bus 1717 from Colégio Militar metro station to Queluz (4 Caminhos), then a 15-minute walk.
directions.parking: Free public parking available near palace entrance

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily except 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January

admissionPrices.notes: Palace and Gardens: adults 18-64 13 euros, youths 6-17 and seniors 65+ 10 euros, children under 6 free, family (2 adults + 2 youths) 35 euros. Gardens only: adults 6 euros, youths and seniors 4.50 euros, family 15 euros. Online tickets are sold for a specific date. Ticket office closed 12:00-13:00; ticket machines available.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Morning, so that the return journey is not squeezed against all-aboard. The gardens are at their best in spring and early summer.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Buy a dated Palace and Gardens ticket on the official Parques de Sintra site before you sail. Take the Sintra-line train from Rossio to Queluz-Belas and walk 10 to 15 minutes, or take a taxi. Allow 1.5 to 2 hours on site. Last admission is 17:30.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: At least 5 hours ashore by taxi or 6 hours by train (50-60 minutes each way plus 1.5-2 hours on site)
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Moderate: metro, a 20-minute train and a 10 to 15-minute walk on town pavements, or a 25 to 30-minute taxi. The site is flat compared with Sintra, but the gardens have steps between levels.
combinableWith: Baixa and Rossio (on the way back)
Belém (by taxi, on calls of 8 hours or more)
tips: Buy a dated Palace and Gardens ticket (13 euros) on the official Parques de Sintra site before you sail; the gardens-only ticket leaves out the reason to come.
Rossio to Queluz-Belas is a two-zone journey: 1.85 euros single on CP's January 2026 price list, or pay with Zapping credit on a 0.50-euro Navegante card.
Monte Abraão, the next station towards Sintra, is about the same distance from the palace if that train comes first.
Last admission to the palace and gardens is 17:30. The ticket desk closes from 12:00 to 13:00, but the ticket machines keep working.
Download Parques de Sintra's Zoomguide audio guide or Queluz Maps app before you leave the ship.
Closed 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January; Parques de Sintra monuments can also close at short notice for state events.
Leave Queluz at least 2 hours before all-aboard if you return by train; a taxi back takes 25 to 30 minutes, longer at weekday rush hours.
Do not try to combine Queluz with Pena on the same port day.

highlights: Throne Room, with gilded carving, mirrors and chandeliers
Music Room and Ambassadors Room, the main reception rooms of the 18th-century court
Don Quixote Room, where Pedro IV was born in 1798 and died in 1834
Tiled Corridor, lined with azulejo panels
Tiled Canal in the gardens, lined with blue-and-white azulejos
Grand Cascade and the Medallions Lake
Upper Gardens with lead statues from John Cheere's London workshop
facilities: Palace shop with souvenirs and books

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Gardens fully accessible with ramps and paved paths. Palace interior has some stairs and limited wheelchair access - ground floor accessible. Wheelchairs available on request. Accessible restrooms available
accessibility.visualAidServices: Audio guides available in multiple languages
